title: Support New AI Frameworks Faster Using NVIDIA Workload Map | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA open-sourced Workload Map (formerly Karta, Apache 2.0) as part of its DSX AI Factory Platform: a Kubernetes CRD plus Go library that describes distributed workload structure declaratively so schedulers and platforms need no per-framework adapters. It ships definitions for 13 workload types and is used by Run:ai, KAI Scheduler and Elotl's Nova.

themes.theme: Per-CRD adapter problem in Kubernetes AI

insights.claim: On Kubernetes, each AI framework encodes workload structure differently, so schedulers, controllers, dashboards and cost tools need a separate adapter per custom resource to interpret components, pod templates, replica counts and status.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Integration overhead slows adoption of new AI frameworks on GPU clusters.

insights.claim: The authors argue per-framework adapter development becomes a recurring roadmap item rather than a one-time cost, which is why support for new workload types often waits for a product release.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Declarative definitions could shorten time-to-support for new AI frameworks on platforms.
insights.quote: That makes adapter development a roadmap item per framework, not a one-time cost
insights.locator: A developer answers those questions once

insights.claim: Without a workload definition, NVIDIA Run:ai displayed a JobSet's component Jobs as three separate workloads of four GPUs each rather than one 12-GPU workload.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Fragmented visibility hampers GPU accounting and quota management.

insights.claim: Workload Map, formerly Karta, ships as a Kubernetes CRD plus a Go library where each definition specifies where to find pod templates, replica counts and status fields for a workload type.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Workload knowledge becomes data rather than compiled code.

insights.claim: Workload Map moves workload knowledge out of compiled adapters into declarative YAML data that developers can write, review and apply to a cluster like any other manifest.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Lowers the cost for ecosystem tools to support arbitrary AI frameworks.
insights.quote: workload knowledge moves out of compiled adapters and into data developers can write, review, and apply to a cluster like any other manifest
insights.locator: The key is that workload knowledge

insights.claim: Workload Map ships prebuilt, tested definitions for JobSet, PyTorchJob, RayCluster, RayJob, RayService, KServe, Knative, MPIJob, NVIDIA NIM, LeaderWorkerSet, Milvus, Grove PodCliqueSet and NVIDIA Dynamo.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Broad coverage of training and inference frameworks out of the box.

insights.claim: Status mappings translate heterogeneous framework statuses into a shared vocabulary, e.g. deriving JobSet 'Running' via a jq expression because JobSet reports no plain Running condition.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Uniform status enables cross-framework dashboards and automation.

insights.claim: A single JobSet definition is reused by the Workload Map CLI for inspection, by KAI Scheduler for gang scheduling, and by NVIDIA Run:ai for unified workload management.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Reinforces NVIDIA's software layer as the common control plane for AI factories.

insights.claim: KAI Scheduler uses Workload Map as a fallback in its pod grouper for workload types without a native plugin, while native plugins retain precedence.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Gang scheduling becomes available for new frameworks without new scheduler code.

insights.claim: In NVIDIA Run:ai a single API call registers a new workload type using a catalog definition with no additional code.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Faster onboarding of customer frameworks strengthens Run:ai's platform value.
insights.locator: In NVIDIA Run:ai, a single API call

insights.claim: Workload Map is available under the Apache 2.0 license and is used in production within NVIDIA Run:ai.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Open-sourcing production code aims to make NVIDIA's abstraction an ecosystem standard.

insights.claim: Elotl's Nova uses Workload Map to interpret workload structure and resource requirements when choosing a cluster for distributed workloads in multi-cluster scheduling.
insights.speaker: Alon Lavian
insights.so_what: Early third-party adoption signals potential ecosystem standardization.
insights.locator: Adoption also extends to multi-cluster scheduling
